 PLEASE NOTE--The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the Mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

are recommending measures to promote social distancing. If you would like to comment on
any listed Agenda Items or Non-Agenda Items, please email the City Clerk’s office at
publiccomment@hpca.gov or Esarmiento@hpca.gov or by telephone, by calling (323) 584-
6297, up to one (1) hour, prior to the start of the meeting. Public Comments will then be read
during public comment and made part of the record. Below is the virtual link and toll free

 In the interest of Public Health and Safety in order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19
virus, you are strongly encouraged to observe the City Council meetings on the City of
Huntington Park's website at www.hpca.gov or virtually via the Zoom link provided above.

The City of Huntington Park thanks you in advance for your cooperation.

For both open and closed session, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries shall be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

ADDITIONS/DELETIONS TO AGENDA

Items of business may be added to the agenda upon a motion adopted by a minimum two-
thirds vote finding that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action
came to the attention of the City or Agency subsequent to the agenda being posted. Items
may be deleted from the agenda upon the request of staff or Council.

IMPORTANT NOTICE

The City of Huntington Park shows replays of City Council Meetings on Local Access
Channel 3 and over the Internet at www.hpca.gov. NOTE: Your attendance at this public
meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice.

The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
called to order at 6:02 p.m. on Tuesday, February 21, 2023, in the Council Chambers at
City Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Eduardo “Eddie”
Martinez presiding.

PRESENT: Councilmember(s): Graciela Ortiz, Karina Macias, Arturo Flores, Vice Mayor
Marilyn Sanabria and Mayor Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez.

ABSENT: None

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: City Manager Ricardo Reyes; Cesar Roldan Director of Public
Works; Raul Alvarez Assistant City Manager; Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk; Cosme
Lozano Police Chief, John Balderas, Finance Manager; Steve Foster Director of
Community Development; Sergio Infanzon Director of Communications; Araceli Almazan
City Attorney, Cynthia Norzagaray Director of Parks & Recreation -Absent.

INVOCATION

Invocation was led by Mayor Martinez.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Martinez.

PRESENTATION(S)

1.  CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION TO THE WRESTLING GUY STORE
  CELEBRATING TEN YEARS OF BUSINESS IN HUNTINGTON PARK
2.  CERTIFICATE OF APPRECIATION TO SURF BUS FOUNDATION
3.  CERTIFICATE OF APPRECIATION TO PACIFIC ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
  TEACHERS
4.  PROCLAMATION FOR WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following members of the public provided public comment:
1. Dorothy Lowe
2. Yatoyo Toy
3. Alejandro Villapando
4. Christian Contreras
5. Ebonique (No last name given)
6. Kevin Cervantes
 7. Yvonne Correa
8. Maricela Talamantes
9. Francisco Rivera

STAFF RESPONSE

City Attorney Araceli Almazan addressed the public comments related to Anthony Lowe.
She stated that due to this being an active investigation the City and City Council are not
in any position to comment on the facts regarding the ongoing investigation. She then
clarified that the city upon receipt of a claim has a number of days to reject that claim and
if it is not rejected within a very specific number of days it is deemed rejected by
operation of law at which point council can file a lawsuit as it relates to the matter
discussed during public comment.

Police Chief Lozano provided a response related the 58th Street alley. He shared that the
police department continues to police that alley a minimum of three times per 24 hour
period. When officers contact the individual’s in the alley they are not involved in any
criminal activity but police do clear the area because loitering is not permitted. Once
officers leave the area the individuals return. He added that in addition to the patrols,
police are also dispatched to the area when calls are received from residents. Then
addressed the property line that has been marked off to identify private property. He
stated that property owners should call police and report any intrusions onto private
property. He then addressed the comment related how many patrol personnel. He stated
that the Police Department does deploy an adequate amount of police personnel into the
community. This includes patrol officers, parking enforcement, and public safety officers.
He added that the Police Department also has an agreement with the Police Officers
Union that mandate a certain number of officers be deployed per shift with varying ranks
and specialized teams that work with and augment police presence in the community. He
closed by sharing that the Police Department operates on a standing mutual aid
agreement with neighboring departments and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
department that can deploy at a moments notice.

CLOSSED SESSION

City Attorney Araceli Almazan stated that it is appropriate to recess to closed

session. Mayor Martinez recessed into closed session at 7:25 p.m.

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Police Chief Cosme Lozano announced that the next meet your police meeting is
scheduled for Thursday March 30, 2023 at 6:00pm at the Salt Lake Park Community
Center. He encouraged everyone to attend the event. He also shared that applications
are being accepted for the police explorer program for children.

Director of Community Development Steve Forster advise that the minor home repair
program is live on the city’s website. He added that this is an opportunity for community
members to apply for grant funding for up to $25,000 for minor home repairs. He also
mentioned that first-time home buyer workshops continue to be held and encouraged
everyone to attend.

Communications Director Sergio Infanzon shared information on upcoming events and
available resources provided in the Huntington Park newsletter.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

None

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Councilmember Ortiz requested staff address the potholes that were caused by the
excessive rain. She also requested a status update regarding the statues at Veteran Park
and the Huntington Park signage that was damaged by a commuter. She then requested
staff conduct an audit of all the slides and swings at the local parks. She concluded her
 comments by thanking staff for their efforts.

Councilmember Macias thanked staff, employees, and her colleagues for all their hard
work and wished everyone a good night.

Councilmember Flores thanked all the staff who participated in the Veterans brunch
event. He added that he received good feedback and has received multiple requests
from surrounding city’s that would like to participate next year.

Vice Mayor Sanabria reminded everyone in the community about Earth Day on April 15,
2023. She added that historically bulky item pick ups have been offered and will continue
this year. She asked everyone who plans to participate please plan ahead and make
sure items are put out by Friday April 14, 2023 at 6:00pm to ensure prompt pick up. She
closed by thanking everyone for all their hard work.

Mayor Martinez thanked staff for always keeping everyone safe and providing a health
environment. He then requested staff investigate the signage at Florence near Salt Lake
Park because the lights around the sign don’t seem to be functioning.

ADJOURNMENT
Mayor Martinez adjourned the meeting in memory of Ramon Salvador Gonzalez at 8:31
p.m. The next City of Huntington Park City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday
March 21, 2023 at 6:00 pm

Respectfully submitted

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
